# boundaries

Rules about dependencies between elements and on packages and globals.

| Rule                                                  | Description                                                           | Default level |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| [allowed-imports](#allowed-imports)                   | Controls which elements may import which.                             | `error`       |
| [entry-only](#entry-only)                             | Imports from outside an element must target its entry files.          | `error`       |
| [no-cycles](#no-cycles)                               | Elements must not depend on each other in a cycle.                    | `error`       |
| [no-entry-import](#no-entry-import)                   | Imports must target the files they need, not entry files.             | `error`       |
| [no-orphans](#no-orphans)                             | Source files must be imported by non-test code, or be an entry point. | `warn`        |
| [no-undeclared-dependency](#no-undeclared-dependency) | Imported packages must be declared in the nearest package.json.       | `error`       |
| [no-unresolved](#no-unresolved)                       | Imports must resolve to a file or an installed package.               | `error`       |
| [public-api](#public-api)                             | Imported files of an element must be reachable from its entry files.  | `error`       |
| [restricted-globals](#restricted-globals)             | Globals, or members of globals, that must not be used.                | `error`       |
| [restricted-packages](#restricted-packages)           | Packages, or names from packages, that must not be imported.          | `error`       |

## allowed-imports

Controls which elements may import which.

- **Id:** `boundaries/allowed-imports`
- **Default level:** `error`

Each rule matches the importing file with `from`. A target that matches `disallow` is
reported. When a matching rule has `allow`, targets that match no `allow` list are reported.
Otherwise `default` decides: `allow` (the default) or `disallow`. Imports inside one element
are allowed, except where a `disallow` selector with only `files` matches. Selectors are
element types, or `{ type, captures, files }`.

To fix a finding, move the shared code to a place both sides may import, or invert the
dependency so the lower-level code does not know about the higher-level code.

### Options

```ts
{
  rules: {
    from: Selector[] | Selector;
    allow?: Selector[] | Selector;
    disallow?: Selector[] | Selector;
    message?: string;
    hint?: string;
  }[];
  default?: 'allow' | 'disallow';
  includeTests?: boolean;
  ignoreTypeImports?: boolean;
}
```

| Option              | Type                     | Default   | Description                                                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rules`             | `object[]`               | required  | Rules, checked in order.                                            |
| `rules[].from`      | `Selector[] \| Selector` | required  | Files whose imports this rule checks.                               |
| `rules[].allow`     | `Selector[] \| Selector` |           | The only targets these files may import, besides their own element. |
| `rules[].disallow`  | `Selector[] \| Selector` |           | Targets these files must not import.                                |
| `rules[].message`   | `string`                 |           | Replaces the finding message, for example to explain the rule.      |
| `rules[].hint`      | `string`                 |           | Shown under the finding as the next step.                           |
| `default`           | `'allow' \| 'disallow'`  | `'allow'` | Whether imports between elements that no rule mentions are allowed. |
| `includeTests`      | `boolean`                | `false`   | Also check imports from test files.                                 |
| `ignoreTypeImports` | `boolean`                | `false`   | Skip imports that only import types.                                |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/allowed-imports': [
    'error',
    {
      rules: [
        { from: 'feature', allow: ['common', 'shared'] },
        {
          from: 'common',
          disallow: 'feature',
          message: 'Common code must not know features.',
          hint: 'Pass what the common code needs in as an argument.',
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
},
```

## entry-only

Imports from outside an element must target its entry files.

- **Id:** `boundaries/entry-only`
- **Default level:** `error`

An element exposes its public API through its entry files (`entry` in the element
definition, `index.ts` by default). Code outside the element must not reach into its
other files, so the element can change its internals freely.

To fix a finding, export what you need from the entry file and import it from there.
Test files are skipped unless `includeTests` is set.

### Options

```ts
{
  elements: Selector[] | Selector;
  includeTests?: boolean;
  ignoreTypeImports?: boolean;
}
```

| Option              | Type                     | Default  | Description                                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `elements`          | `Selector[] \| Selector` | required | Elements that must be imported through their entry files. |
| `includeTests`      | `boolean`                | `false`  | Also check imports from test files.                       |
| `ignoreTypeImports` | `boolean`                | `false`  | Skip imports that only import types.                      |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/entry-only': ['error', { elements: ['feature', 'common'] }],
},
```

## no-cycles

Elements must not depend on each other in a cycle.

- **Id:** `boundaries/no-cycles`
- **Default level:** `error`

A cycle between elements means none of them can be understood, tested, or moved on its
own. The finding shows the import that closes the cycle and the other imports in it.

To fix a finding, move the shared code into an element both can depend on, or invert one
of the dependencies, for example by passing a callback instead of importing.

### Options

```ts
{
  elements?: Selector[] | Selector;
  includeTests?: boolean;
  ignoreTypeImports?: boolean;
}
```

| Option              | Type                     | Default | Description                                   |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `elements`          | `Selector[] \| Selector` |         | Elements to check. Defaults to every element. |
| `includeTests`      | `boolean`                | `false` | Also check imports from test files.           |
| `ignoreTypeImports` | `boolean`                | `false` | Skip imports that only import types.          |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/no-cycles': ['error', { ignoreTypeImports: true }],
},
```

## no-entry-import

Imports must target the files they need, not entry files.

- **Id:** `boundaries/no-entry-import`
- **Default level:** `error`

Entry files often load a whole element, including UI and hooks. Some code must import
the specific files it needs instead: code inside an element importing its own entry
(`to: "self"`), or elements that only need a model or helper from another element.

To fix a finding, import the file that defines what you use.

### Options

```ts
{
  rules: {
    from: Selector[] | Selector;
    to: 'self' | Selector[] | Selector;
    message?: string;
  }[];
  includeTests?: boolean;
}
```

| Option            | Type                               | Default  | Description                                                                                       |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rules`           | `object[]`                         | required |                                                                                                   |
| `rules[].from`    | `Selector[] \| Selector`           | required | Files whose imports this rule checks.                                                             |
| `rules[].to`      | `'self' \| Selector[] \| Selector` | required | Elements whose entry files must not be imported, or `self` for the element of the importing file. |
| `rules[].message` | `string`                           |          | Replaces the finding message, for example to explain the rule.                                    |
| `includeTests`    | `boolean`                          | `false`  | Also check imports from test files.                                                               |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/no-entry-import': [
    'error',
    {
      rules: [
        { from: 'feature', to: 'self' },
        {
          from: 'common',
          to: 'common',
          message: 'Import only the files you need.',
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
},
```

## no-orphans

Source files must be imported by non-test code, or be an entry point.

- **Id:** `boundaries/no-orphans`
- **Default level:** `warn`

A file that only tests import is usually left over from a refactor. Entry files of elements,
test files, declaration files, config files, and files matching `roots` are entry points
and are never reported. List other entry points, such as `src/main.ts` or CLI scripts, in
`roots`.

To fix a finding, delete the file if it is unused, import it where it is needed, or add it
to `roots` if it is an entry point.

### Options

```ts
{
  roots?: string[];
}
```

| Option  | Type       | Default | Description                                                         |
| ------- | ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `roots` | `string[]` | `[]`    | Globs of entry points, such as `src/main.ts`, that nothing imports. |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/no-orphans': ['warn', { roots: ['src/main.ts', 'scripts/**'] }],
},
```

## no-undeclared-dependency

Imported packages must be declared in the nearest package.json.

- **Id:** `boundaries/no-undeclared-dependency`
- **Default level:** `error`

A package that is imported but not declared works only by accident, through hoisting or
another package. Imports of workspace packages must be declared too.

devDependencies count for test files and for files matching `allowDev`. Type-only imports
also accept the matching `@types` package.

To fix a finding, add the package to the nearest package.json.

### Options

```ts
{
  allowDev?: string[];
  ignore?: string[];
}
```

| Option     | Type       | Default                              | Description                                                         |
| ---------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allowDev` | `string[]` | `['**/*.config.*', '**/scripts/**']` | Globs of files that may import devDependencies, besides test files. |
| `ignore`   | `string[]` | `[]`                                 | Package names or globs that are never reported.                     |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/no-undeclared-dependency': [
    'error',
    { allowDev: ['**/*.config.*', 'scripts/**'], ignore: ['virtual:*'] },
  ],
},
```

## no-unresolved

Imports must resolve to a file or an installed package.

- **Id:** `boundaries/no-unresolved`
- **Default level:** `error`

An import that cannot be resolved usually points at a moved or deleted file, a typo, or a
package that is not installed. Resolution follows the nearest tsconfig.json, including
`paths`. Imports of files excluded from the project are not reported.

To fix a finding, correct the path, or install the missing package.

### Options

```ts
{
  ignore?: string[];
}
```

| Option   | Type       | Default | Description                                                              |
| -------- | ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ignore` | `string[]` | `[]`    | Globs of import specifiers that are never reported, such as `virtual:*`. |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/no-unresolved': [
    'error',
    { ignore: ['virtual:*', '*.svg?react'] },
  ],
},
```

## public-api

Imported files of an element must be reachable from its entry files.

- **Id:** `boundaries/public-api`
- **Default level:** `error`

Some elements allow imports of individual files, as long as those files are part of the
public API: reachable from an entry file through re-exports, directly or through other
barrels. The rule checks files, not individual exported names.

To fix a finding, export the file from the element entry (or a barrel it re-exports), or
import something that is already public.

### Options

```ts
{
  elements: Selector[] | Selector;
  from?: Selector[] | Selector;
  exceptions?: {
    from?: Selector[] | Selector;
    to: string | string[];
  }[];
  includeTests?: boolean;
}
```

| Option              | Type                     | Default  | Description                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `elements`          | `Selector[] \| Selector` | required | Elements whose imported files must be part of their public API.         |
| `from`              | `Selector[] \| Selector` |          | Files whose imports are checked. Defaults to files outside the element. |
| `exceptions`        | `object[]`               | `[]`     | Imports that are allowed even though the file is not public.            |
| `exceptions[].from` | `Selector[] \| Selector` |          | Importing files. Defaults to any file.                                  |
| `exceptions[].to`   | `string \| string[]`     | required | Globs of files that may be imported anyway.                             |
| `includeTests`      | `boolean`                | `false`  | Also check imports from test files.                                     |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/public-api': [
    'error',
    {
      elements: 'common',
      exceptions: [{ from: 'feature', to: 'src/common/*/models/**' }],
    },
  ],
},
```

## restricted-globals

Globals, or members of globals, that must not be used.

- **Id:** `boundaries/restricted-globals`
- **Default level:** `error`

Import rules cannot see globals such as `fetch`, `process`, `Date.now`, or `Math.random`.
This rule finds them in the code, including `globalThis.fetch`. A name declared in the
file, for example a parameter called `fetch`, is not the global and is not reported.
Restrictions can apply to some elements or files only, for example to keep utils pure.

To fix a finding, pass the value in, or move the code to a place where it is allowed.

### Options

```ts
{
  globals: {
    name: string;
    from?: Selector[] | Selector;
    message?: string;
    hint?: string;
  }[];
}
```

| Option              | Type                     | Default  | Description                                                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `globals`           | `object[]`               | required | The restricted globals.                                                   |
| `globals[].name`    | `string`                 | required | A global such as `fetch` or `process`, or a member such as `Date.now`.    |
| `globals[].from`    | `Selector[] \| Selector` |          | Files the restriction applies to. Defaults to every file.                 |
| `globals[].message` | `string`                 |          | Added to the finding message, for example the reason for the restriction. |
| `globals[].hint`    | `string`                 |          | Shown under the finding as the next step.                                 |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/restricted-globals': [
    'error',
    {
      globals: [
        {
          name: 'fetch',
          from: { files: '**/utils/**' },
          message: 'Utils are pure functions.',
        },
        {
          name: 'Date.now',
          from: { files: '**/utils/**' },
          hint: 'Pass the time in.',
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
},
```

## restricted-packages

Packages, or names from packages, that must not be imported.

- **Id:** `boundaries/restricted-packages`
- **Default level:** `error`

Restrictions keep code on the libraries the project has chosen, for example the design
system instead of a component library it wraps, or away from a library being phased out.
A restriction can cover a whole package, some names from it, or only some elements.
Node builtins are matched as `node:<name>`, for example to keep `node:fs` out of pure code.

To fix a finding, use the alternative named in the message.

### Options

```ts
{
  packages: {
    name: string;
    importNames?: string[];
    allowTypeImports?: boolean;
    from?: Selector[] | Selector;
    message?: string;
    hint?: string;
  }[];
}
```

| Option                        | Type                     | Default  | Description                                                               |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages`                    | `object[]`               | required | The restricted packages.                                                  |
| `packages[].name`             | `string`                 | required | Package name or glob, such as `@mui/material`, `lodash*`, or `node:fs`.   |
| `packages[].importNames`      | `string[]`               |          | Only these imported names are restricted. Defaults to the whole package.  |
| `packages[].allowTypeImports` | `boolean`                | `false`  | Allow imports that only import types.                                     |
| `packages[].from`             | `Selector[] \| Selector` |          | Files the restriction applies to. Defaults to every file.                 |
| `packages[].message`          | `string`                 |          | Added to the finding message, for example the reason for the restriction. |
| `packages[].hint`             | `string`                 |          | Shown under the finding as the next step.                                 |

### Example

```ts
rules: {
  'boundaries/restricted-packages': [
    'error',
    {
      packages: [
        {
          name: '@mui/material',
          importNames: ['Button'],
          message: 'Use the design system instead.',
          hint: 'Import Button from @acme/design-system.',
        },
        { name: 'node:{fs,child_process}', from: { files: '**/utils/**' } },
      ],
    },
  ],
},
```

## Types

Types used by the options above.

### Selector

An element type, or an object that matches elements by type and captures, or files by glob. All given fields must match.

```ts
type Selector =
  | string
  | {
      type?: string;
      captures?: Record<string, string | string[]>;
      files?: string | string[];
    };
```

| Field      | Type                                 | Default | Description                                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `type`     | `string`                             |         | Element type.                                                                  |
| `captures` | `Record<string, string \| string[]>` |         | Allowed values per capture of the element pattern, such as `{ name: "auth" }`. |
| `files`    | `string \| string[]`                 |         | Globs matched against file paths.                                              |
